label: a b appeared earlier in the input (strongest when b is the first token); input phase and <DEL> only
explanation: Fires only during the original-input phase from step 2 on and at the <DEL> step. It is almost silent in the copy phase (0.2% of mass) and never fires at t=0 or 1. Most of its activation mass comes from sequences in which the letter b was already input. When b is the first original token, the feature fires at essentially every step from t=2 through <DEL> (precision 0.998, 41% of mass); every top example starts with b. If b shows up later in the sequence, the response is weaker. A few other early letters (z, l, m) raise it a little. Separately, the feature has a weak, broad baseline: small activations at many input-phase and <DEL> steps of sequences with no b, mostly on first occurrences of a token. This is why recall is only about 0.42. Adding z and l to the seen-set lifts mass recall to 0.92 but drops precision to 0.45. Magnitude is largest when b is the first token, peaks around t=3-6 and at <DEL>, and falls off in the copy phase.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: b, z, l, m, h, k; least: o, c, t, x) and the second original token (most: b, z, l, m, h, w; least: 1, x, c, t); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=6, t=4.
